Title 1: VAR-E01 | Understand a synthetic offside goal review
Description:
Backlog revision: 0.2, 2026-10-21. Prototype contract remains 0.1. Proposed; no implementation or user validation claimed.

User story: As a football viewer, I want to explore what happened, which evidence mattered and why a controlled variation changes the interpretation, so that I understand the review without treating AI as the referee.

Scope: One synthetic offside-related goal-review family, S1 complete evidence, S2 one changed position fact, S3 missing snapshot. English casual/analyst views; replay; illustrative scene; evidence/rules; explicit authored/live modes; controlled comparison; recap. Excludes real footage, general adjudication, open chat, accounts, payments and production hosting.

Business requirements: BR-01 synthetic/provisional labels; BR-02 separate original decision, supplied review outcome and explanation; BR-03 three evidence variants; BR-04 inspectable evidence/rules; BR-05 referenced claims; BR-06 audience consistency; BR-07 reversible comparison; BR-08 honest limitations/errors; BR-09 usable replay and supplied consequence; BR-10 observable verification.

Acceptance criteria:

  1. [VAR-E01-AC1] All three scenarios complete the core journey, with the comparison available only for the supported pair.
  2. [VAR-E01-AC2] Explanations expose valid evidence and rule references; missing decisive evidence never becomes a definitive offside conclusion.
  3. [VAR-E01-AC3] Authored and live-model output are visibly distinguished; at least one authorised live request succeeds through the actual application.
  4. [VAR-E01-AC4] The integrated prototype passes its recorded automated and browser checks, including keyboard use and 375px and 1280px viewport widths.
  5. [VAR-E01-AC5] Run instructions, limitations, source-review status and actual verification results are available; unperformed user research is marked not run.

Delivery: G00 shared baseline precedes eight independent implementation packages, VAR-101 through VAR-108. G01 integration depends on all eight and authorised model access. Authored-only is an intermediate milestone, not epic completion. A technically complete prototype does not validate commercial demand.

Learning hypothesis: Compare the app with a short written explanation in a five-viewer pilot; target four viewers correctly explaining a new example. This is a proposed exploratory target, not measured evidence or a mandatory completed study for technical acceptance.

Planning source: docs/backlog/README.md and docs/backlog/contract-v0.1.md. All items are initially unapproved for dispatch. CSV is a creation snapshot; do not import it twice.

Technical breakdown: 22 technical Tasks are children of the 10 Issues; 33 work items in total. See docs/backlog/technical-tasks.md. Parent Issues remain the independent agent assignments after the shared gate; child completion prerequisites are explicit.
